comparison: Perfect match on claims C52-C61 regarding the αV24Y T20S structure being in an open state. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the structural data convincing and well-supported, with peer reviewers noting the analysis is comprehensive and technically sound.

Perfect match on claims C62-C69 regarding structural and mechanistic differences between αV24Y and ZYA-T20S. Both evaluations support these conformational change measurements without challenge, with peer reviewers confirming technical soundness.

Strong overlap on core mechanistic conclusions (C3, C5, C6, C49, C72, C76). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers affirm the central finding that Hb pocket occupancy is sufficient for gate opening. Editor describes evidence as 'convincing' and reviewers note data are 'solid' and 'technically sound.'

Both address pocket widening measurements (C73-C76) and mechanistic conclusions. OpenEval also includes C136-C140 on allosteric propagation. Peer reviewers accept the structural measurements and mechanistic interpretations without challenge, describing evidence as convincing.

Both address the comprehensive mechanistic model (C136-C140) of how local changes propagate to global conformational changes. OpenEval evaluates this as supported inference from structural data; peer reviewers accept without challenge, noting technical soundness.

Both address αK66's role (C70-C71). OpenEval finds this novel observation well-supported by structural comparison. Peer reviewers accept the finding, with Reviewer 1 noting it brings 'new emphasis' to this residue. Peer result R4 also includes additional claims C7, C100-C106 not in OpenEval R3.

Strong overlap on αK66's mechanistic role (C99-C106). OpenEval emphasizes the combination of structural and biochemical validation supporting a novel conclusion. Peer reviewers accept this finding as supported by mutations, describing evidence as convincing.

Both address comparative structural analysis of hydrophobic groups and HbYX motif roles (C90-C98). OpenEval finds the distinction between allosteric effects and binding affinity well-supported. Peer reviewers accept without challenge, noting alignment with existing literature.

Strong overlap on αV24F mutant structural phenotype (C111-C116). OpenEval finds observations supported despite unexpected nature. Peer reviewers accept without challenge. Peer result R7 also includes assembly implications (C131-C133) that OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Both address assembly findings from αV24F data (C131-C133). OpenEval finds the unexpected observation about partial assembly well-supported. Peer reviewers accept without challenge, describing evidence as convincing.

Strong overlap on sequence conservation and translatability (C124-C130). OpenEval finds conservation analysis supports potential translatability while noting mammalian complexity. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about extrapolation to eukaryotic systems, with editor and Reviewer 1 noting this 'may prove challenging.'

Both address translatability claims (C50-C51, C122-C123). OpenEval finds these supported by citations and established knowledge. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about extrapolation to more complex eukaryotic proteasomes, despite accepting the archaeal data.
